facts.activity_file: responding to slope-radar and prism alarms

control_failures.control_label: benching, battering or shoring of an excavation
inspection and monitoring of highwalls and batters

hazard_media: stored potential of an elevated component
facts.site: Yandarra Downs Open Cut and Heavy Workshop
facts.title: unrelieved potential energy found after isolation of DZ-9201

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was no injury or loss. The potential outcome was rated 2 against the site's consequence scale, above the 0 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control EXCAVATION_SUPPORT: the benching, battering or shoring of an excavation had degraded below its design intent, and the learning team review classified this as an absent or failed defence.

Control GROUND_CONDITION_INSPECTION: the inspection and monitoring of highwalls and batters had degraded below its design intent, and the learning team review classified this as a task or environmental condition.
Control SLOPE_MONITORING_RESPONSE: the response to slope monitoring alarms was in place but did not perform, and the learning team review classified this as a task or environmental condition.

recommendations: Restore the benching, battering or shoring of an excavation on DZ-9201 and record the assurance activity before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in monitoring and inspecting ground conditions, specifically responding to slope-radar and prism alarms. DZ-9201 (earthmoving fleet) is in service for loading and dozing. The task proceeded during start-up after maintenance while the benching, battering or shoring of an excavation had degraded below its design intent. The gravity energy involved is held as suspended load, and the recorded presentation was fall, collapse, crush.
response.summary: On 30 August 2024 a high potential incident was recorded on DZ-9201 at Yandarra Downs Open Cut and Heavy Workshop during start-up after maintenance; gravity energy held as suspended load was not released.
